messages:
elaine: Quick sync — we need a practical proposal for max batch tokens per GPU (A10/T4/L4/A100/H100). Seeing KV cache pressure + kernel fallback regressions in last canary. Thoughts?

mike: Agree, perf regressions started after the kernel selector change last week. H100s look fine but A10/T4 tails spiked. suspect fallback to generic attention kernel when kv cache gets fragmented. :frowning: 

chitra: Posting short perf summary from yesterday's profile:
```
perf-bucket: run=2026-02-12
model=redwood-13b
hw=A10
median p50=72ms p95=420ms
kv-cache hitratio=0.78
kernel=optimized_attn_small_seq (fallback 14% -> generic)
```
Problem: batched requests with varying prefix lengths cause different KV segment layouts, which pushes some contexts to fallback path.

sam: My take — tighten token-budget target per-device to reduce heterogeneity in batch formation. Right now continuous-batching uses global token_budget=12000 which is too high for T4/A10. Suggest per-GPU defaults: T4=6k, A10=8k, L4=9k, A100=16k, H100=20k. These reduce mix of short+very-long in same micro-batch and reduce kernel fallbacks.

elaine: Those numbers sound reasonable. Can we simulate impact quickly? If we lower T4 to 6k, how does throughput vs latency change? Any regressions on cost?

perf-bot: quick sim results (approx):
- T4 token_budget=12k -> throughput 540 tok/s, p95 680ms
- T4 token_budget=6k  -> throughput 510 tok/s, p95 340ms
(less tail, slight throughput drop due to smaller aggregation windows)

mike: That's acceptable — we favor tail latency for API SLOs. Also need to tweak queue_policy: prefer length-homogeneous grouping. Current queue is FIFO with timebound=20ms. Suggest heuristic: sort-in-window by prefix_len desc then by arrival. Pseudocode: 
```
window = drain(20ms)
window.sort(key=lambda r: (r.prefix_len_bucket, r.arrival))
form_batches(window, token_budget)
```

chitra: Also call out KV cache eviction behavior. We saw eviction churn when batch included an old context + fresh short prompt, causing extra KV loads. Two mitigations: 1) prefer batch packs with similar cache_age, 2) pin small fraction of KV on LRU grace to avoid immediate eviction for repeats.

sam: Implementation notes:
- Add per-device token_budget config in runtime.yaml.
- Expose metrics: batch_token_count, kernel_fallback_rate, kv_cache_evictions_per_min.
- Add canary: deploy to 5% T4 pool with new T4=6k and queue sort-in-window.

elaine: Sounds good. Mike/Chitra, can you draft the runtime config PR and a perf-checklist for canary? I can own the rollout.

mike: On it — will open PR with config + unit tests for sort-window behaviour. Will include synthetic benchmarks (short/long mix) and a small script to compute kernel_fallback_rate from pprof traces.

chitra: I'll add KV metrics and the eviction alert (pager at >50 evict/min in dedicated pools).

perf-bot: checklist reminder: run 1000-sample end-to-end with seeded workload (mix: 60% short<128 30% mid 128-1024 10% long>1024) and compare p95/throughput/kernel_fallback.

elaine: Great. If canary looks good, rollout plan: T4 -> A10 -> L4 -> A100 -> H100 over 72h with rollback gates on kernel_fallback_rate or p95 increase >10%.

sam: Minor note: for L4 we might leave token_budget slightly higher than A10 because its INT8 path handles mixed lengths better. Proposed L4=9k stands.

mike: PR draft ready by EOD. tagging @elaine for rollout ops once perf checks are green. :rocket:
